subject: sst
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF
note: The unnumbered "Introduction: Why Social Science?" is not listed as a chapter.

chapters.title: Locating Places on the Earth
chapters.theme: Theme A — India and the World: Land and the People

topics.title: Locating Places on the Earth
outcomes: Learner can use latitude, longitude, maps and globes to locate places, including the Prime Meridian and the Ujjain meridian
misconceptions: Thinks latitude lines and longitude lines are the same thing
hooks: Find your town on a map using its coordinates on a phone

chapters.title: Oceans and Continents
chapters.theme: Theme A — India and the World: Land and the People

topics.title: Oceans and Continents
outcomes: Learner can name and locate the continents and oceans and describe how they shape life
hooks: Trace the sea route from Kochi to Africa

chapters.title: Landforms and Life
chapters.theme: Theme A — India and the World: Land and the People

topics.title: Landforms and Life
outcomes: Learner can describe mountains, plateaus and plains and how people live in each
hooks: Compare life in Shimla, the Deccan plateau and the Gangetic plains

chapters.title: Timeline and Sources of History
chapters.theme: Theme B — Tapestry of the Past

topics.title: Timeline and Sources of History
outcomes: Learner can read a timeline using BCE/CE and identify sources historians use (archaeology, texts, inscriptions)
misconceptions: Thinks BCE years count upward like CE years
hooks: Make a timeline of your own family

chapters.title: India, That Is Bharat
chapters.theme: Theme B — Tapestry of the Past

topics.title: India, That Is Bharat
outcomes: Learner can explain the names used for India over time and what they tell us about its past
hooks: Why the Constitution says "India, that is Bharat"

chapters.title: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation
chapters.theme: Theme B — Tapestry of the Past

topics.title: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation
outcomes: Learner can describe features of the Harappan (Sindhu-Sarasvati) civilisation such as town planning, trade and crafts
hooks: The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro and the dockyard at Lothal

chapters.title: India’s Cultural Roots
chapters.theme: Theme C — Our Cultural Heritage and Knowledge Traditions

topics.title: India’s Cultural Roots
outcomes: Learner can describe early knowledge traditions and schools of thought in India, including the Vedas, Buddhism and Jainism
hooks: What does "ahimsa" mean in daily life?

chapters.title: Unity in Diversity, or ‘Many in the One’
chapters.theme: Theme C — Our Cultural Heritage and Knowledge Traditions

topics.title: Unity in Diversity, or ‘Many in the One’
outcomes: Learner can give examples of diversity in language, food, festivals and dress and the shared threads that unite India
hooks: One harvest, many festivals: Pongal, Bihu, Lohri, Makar Sankranti

topics.title: Family and Community
outcomes: Learner can explain how families and communities support members and share responsibilities
hooks: Who does which work at home, and is it fair?

topics.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 1: Governance
outcomes: Learner can explain what governance is and the three organs of government at a basic level
hooks: Who fixes the streetlight on your road?

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas

topics.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas
outcomes: Learner can describe the Panchayati Raj system and the role of the gram sabha
hooks: Attend or role-play a gram sabha meeting

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas

topics.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas
outcomes: Learner can describe the work of municipal bodies and how citizens can participate
hooks: Complaint about a garbage pile: whom do you call?

chapters.title: The Value of Work
chapters.theme: Theme E — Economic Life Around Us

topics.title: The Value of Work
outcomes: Learner can distinguish economic and non-economic activities and value different kinds of work
misconceptions: Thinks unpaid work at home is not "real" work
hooks: List all the work done in your home in a day

chapters.title: Economic Activities Around Us
chapters.theme: Theme E — Economic Life Around Us

topics.title: Economic Activities Around Us
outcomes: Learner can classify economic activities into primary, secondary and tertiary sectors with local examples
hooks: From cotton farm to textile mill to cloth shop
